brief: Goldman's morning wrap (IR KickStart) opens with European equities lower as oil rebounded on Middle East supply threats (Iran stepping up Hormuz ship attacks, Saudi-Houthi tensions), reversing yesterday's move when oil dipped below $98/bbl and eased inflation concerns. Yesterday's rotation: healthcare rose over 2% as European real yields fell, defence gave back gains as Iran-Qatar talks eased tensions, utilities led on the AI power theme while semis lagged on competition concerns. US equities closed at fresh highs (S&P +0.58%, Nasdaq +0.48%) heading into Q3 earnings, though asset manager/hedge fund flows stayed subdued. GS Research projects global AI investment exceeding $1tn this year, with the US and Asia over 80% of data-centre additions and Europe only 10%. Global M&A hit a first-half record ($2.77tn) but Q3 saw the fewest $10bn+ deals since Q4 2024. ISM Services Prices Paid hit 74 (highest since July 2022) on tariffs and fuel costs; record imports widened the US trade deficit, cutting GDPNow to 3.7%. France's Le Pen raised her savings plan to €140bn as the OAT-Bund spread tightened from its post-2011 high, though sovereign-risk concerns persist.
